an3.80:4.2: _Goyāna_ (“cow-cart”) is probably corrupt. Whereas Videha and Kuru were well-known places, no Goyāna is found elsewhere. The Sanskrit spelling is _godānīya_, “cow-donation”, i.e. a land abundant in the wealth typified by cows; the town at its source was called Govardhana, “cow-prosperity”. Now, that word is similar to the name of the famed river Godāvarī ([snp5.1:2.3]()), which arises near modern Mumbai on the west coast. Lands further west were reached by ship from that shore.
an3.80:9.1: The lack of vocative in what follows indicates that this was not addressed to anyone, per Thai editions.
